DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is a nucleic acid that contains the genetic instructions used in the development and functioning of all known living organisms and some viruses. It is made up of molecules called nucleotides, which consist of a phosphate group, a sugar group, and a nitrogen base. The four types of nitrogen bases are adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G), and cytosine (C). The order of these bases determines DNA's instructions, or genetic code. DNA is a double helix formed by base pairs attached to a sugar-phosphate backbone. It serves as the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms, and it can replicate itself.
</answer>
